lines.trans: Did you come running up to me this happily just to collect today's repair payment?
Today I will treat you to a meal, senior.
Turns out Joon-mo remembered everything from that night—did you know too?
Forget it—what fault is it of yours, getting stuck in the middle.
Senior, what is it that you like so much about Senior Joon-mo?
When you like someone, you cannot neatly explain why—what did you like about Hye-joo?
Well, just that she was pretty.
Yet to Joon-mo, I am easygoing, a fun drinking buddy, and comfortable—and I guess that is as far as it goes.
I guess I am just not pretty to him.
You are pretty—you are pretty too, senior!
You have improved a lot lately, Baek Seung-chan—to survive office life, you need to know how to say flattering things too!

examples.trans: Do you have time today?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Did you hear about this today's share?
I was busy today because of today's share.

examples.trans: You are just flattering me to collect today's installment, right? I only have twenty thousand won today.
The topic of payment, settlement came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 이렇다.
Used to emphasize degree.

examples.trans: You can do it like this.
Why is it so cold today?

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to be glad, pleased, or happy to see someone
meanings.note: Commonly used in greetings such as 반갑습니다 or 반가워요.

examples.trans: Nice to meet you.
I was really glad to see my friend after a long time.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너 오늘치 결제 받으려고 이렇게 나한테 반갑게 뛰어온 거야?
examples.trans: Did you come running up to me this happily just to collect today's repair payment?
This expression comes from 'came running'.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.note: Literal meaning: steamed rice.
By extension, refers to a meal in everyday expressions like 밥 먹다 ('to eat a meal').

examples.trans: Have you eaten?
Today's lunch is delicious.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Today I will treat you to a meal, senior.
This expression comes from 'will buy for you (humble)'.

meanings.note: refers to a previously mentioned or specific day

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
I don't have time that day.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'nights' is key.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.
Let's you remember, right? together today.
I worked hard to you remember, right? yesterday too.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 됐어, 넌 무슨 죄니 중간에 껴서.
examples.trans: Forget it—what fault is it of yours, getting stuck in the middle.
Here the word for 'fault is it' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 걔는 어떻게 된 게 중간이 없어, 극단적인 애교!
examples.trans: Somehow she has no middle ground whatsoever—just extreme cuteness!
Here the word for 'middle ground' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 야, 근데 거기 내가 왜 끼냐고?
examples.trans: Hey, why on earth would I get dragged into that?
This expression comes from 'get roped in?'.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
Please don't say it like that.
It's not that difficult compared to what I thought.

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 저런 거지 같은 설명에도 우리 신디가 맞혔다고!
examples.trans: Even with a terrible explanation like that, our Cindy got it right!
Here the word for 'even with an explanation' is key.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: colloquially often pronounced/written 이쁘다

examples.trans: The flowers are really pretty.
This color is prettier.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 근데 준모한테 나는 만만하고 술친구 하기 좋고 편하고 딱 거기까지인가 봐.
examples.trans: Yet to Joon-mo, I am easygoing, a fun drinking buddy, and comfortable—and I guess that is as far as it goes.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold

meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.

pretty clothes
